A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPTIMA framework and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained experiments and proofs can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression, image-classification, calibration, corruption-robustness and augmentation-sensitivity results in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a five-seed SST-5 sentiment-classification experiment in Section 5.4, Table 4.

M1.justification: The augmented likelihood, ELBO and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Section 5.4 adds a discrete token-masking adaptation using REINFORCE gradients to optimize a bounded dropout probability with a Gaussian prior penalty; v1 only described categorical sampling with Gumbel-Softmax.

E1.justification: v2 adds SST-5 five-class sentiment classification with discrete token masking, extending actual evaluation into NLP. Synthetic regression, CIFAR10, CIFAR10-C, SVHN, ImageNet and ImageNet-C coverage is retained, including experiments moved between the main text and appendices.

E2.justification: Existing experiments retain their comparators. The SST-5 comparison adds an explicit Fixed Aug (Matched) control using OPTIMA's learned dropout rate, alongside the already-used comparison families of no augmentation, fixed augmentation and validation-based tuning.

E3.justification: The new NLP protocol fine-tunes DistilBERT for five epochs on the full training split and evaluates accuracy, NLL and ECE, with validation-NLL-based dropout search. Section 5.2 also changes the stated ImageNet backbone from ResNet-50 to ResNet-18, but Table 2 and Appendix E retain ResNet-50, so an actual backbone change is unresolved.

E4.justification: The SST-5 study adds matched-dropout controls and compares prior means of 0.1 and 0.3, examining joint optimization and sensitivity to augmentation preferences. The existing Gaussian-translation analysis varying augmentation count and prior variance is retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, v2 Table 4 reports SST-5 averages over five seeds with plus/minus uncertainty values. Their interpretation as standard deviations or standard errors is unspecified. No increased run count is reported for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds six SST-5 result rows, showing small accuracy differences and performance close to BO-Fixed. Retained CIFAR10 results also change: No Aug/Fixed Aug accuracy rises from 79.69/75.67 to 80.90/80.73, while OPTIMA remains 81.35 and its ECE changes from 0.014 to 0.017 (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 5). Other retained numerical tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Corollary 4.13 asserting calibration-error scaling with augmentation count. Theorem 4.12 and Appendix B.5 explicitly require full-rank posterior covariance. Most remaining mathematical statements, derivations and proofs are retained, with subsequent results renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the claimed empirical validation to NLP and discrete text perturbations. The central contributions concerning Bayesian augmentation selection, joint ELBO optimization and theoretical advantages remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly acknowledges that the posterior assumptions may fail for overparameterized models. The limitations discuss remaining needs in compositional NLP, time-series and multimodal augmentation. The new SST-5 discussion attributes gains to marginal-likelihood optimization rather than dropout tuning, an interpretation absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds dropout parameterization, initialization, prior parameters, learning rates and baseline-selection details. Appendix J newly states that accompanying code is provided, without an access link. Conversely, v1's explicit disclosure of 50 ImageNet predictive Monte Carlo passes is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work adds Mounsaveng et al. (2021) on bilevel optimization and Chatzipantazis et al. (2023) on augmentation distributions. Sanh et al. (2019) and Socher et al. (2013) support the NLP experiment; Gal and Ghahramani (2016) is removed. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: regression and the Bayesian-optimization comparison move from Appendix F into Sections 5.1 and 5.3, while geometric CIFAR10 evaluation and implementation details move into Appendix F.1. Broader impact moves to Appendix I, and limitations and appendix organization are revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds the SST-5 table, redraws CIFAR10 reliability and training/augmentation plots, and relocates existing regression, CIFAR10 and Bayesian-optimization displays. ICLR headers and typography replace the preprint styling, while most table structures and multipanel figure designs are preserved.

improvement.justification: The five-seed SST-5 evaluation and matched-dropout controls provide useful evidence beyond vision, while Section 4.4 makes theoretical restrictions clearer and removes the ECE-scaling claim. These are limited gains: matched-control calibration differences are tiny, the causal attribution to marginalization is stronger than the comparison establishes, and v2 introduces inconsistent ImageNet-backbone and dropout-initialization descriptions. The revision improves empirical breadth and transparency without establishing a substantial overall advance.
